notes: Read the full 196-line numbered source before editing. The module doc (L1-28) describing the browser Fullscreen API wrapper (requestFullscreen/exitFullscreen/fullscreenchange/document.fullscreenEnabled), the targetRef contract, the hide-when-unsupported branch, the fullscreenchange-sourced state, and the aria-label/title/aria-pressed sync is ported into the native file header and re-framed for React Native: the Fullscreen API is entirely DOM-only and UNAVAILABLE on native (rules 4/7), so the native port renders the explicit unavailable state (probeSupport()->false => button hides itself, exactly mirroring the web behaviour when document.fullscreenEnabled is false on iOS Safari / sandboxed iframes).

Imports (L30-34): forwardRef/useCallback/useEffect/useState (react) are kept (React added for jsx:react-native classic runtime). react-i18next useTranslation (L31) -> a local useTranslation fallback hook returning {t} with the same call shape (no react-i18next in apps/native deps; t(key, fallback) resolves to the inline English fallback). lucide-react Maximize/Minimize (L32) -> Unicode glyphs in AppText ('⤢' enter / '⤡' exit) — no lucide on native. cn from @/lib/cn (L33) -> dropped (React Native has no className; styling moves to StyleSheet + tokens; className retained on props for source compatibility and ignored as _className, matching the Badge port). Button from ./Button (L34) -> a Pressable + AppText glyph (the web-parity Button host is not ported; the ghost icon-button visual is reproduced directly with react-native primitives, rule 5).

FullscreenButtonProps (L36-73) is ported field-for-field with JSDoc preserved: targetRef (L42) RefObject<HTMLElement|null> -> RefObject<unknown> (no DOM HTMLElement on native; the .current read is preserved but the toggle is a no-op); ariaLabelEnter (L48) / ariaLabelExit (L53) kept verbatim incl. their t('common.fullscreen.enter'/'exit', ...) default-label JSDoc; className (L59) kept but ignored on native; size (L65) 'sm'|'md'|'lg' kept; testHookSupported (L72) test seam kept verbatim (re-documented as overriding the always-false native probe). Two native-only props are added for parity consumers: style?:StyleProp<ViewStyle> and testID (maps the web data-testid).

probeSupport() (L75-83) -> returns false: React Native has no document and no element-level Fullscreen API, so element fullscreen is always unavailable. This is the rule-7 explicit unavailable state and mirrors the web's own false result on iOS Safari / sandboxed iframes, where the button hides itself. The L76 `typeof document === 'undefined'` SSR guard and the L82 `document.fullscreenEnabled === true` probe are subsumed into the unconditional false. readFullscreenElement() (L85-88) -> returns null: there is never an active fullscreen element on native; the L86 SSR guard and L87 `document.fullscreenElement ?? null` are subsumed into the unconditional null.

Component doc + signature (L90-101): forwardRef<HTMLButtonElement, FullscreenButtonProps> -> forwardRef<View, FullscreenButtonProps> (Pressable's host ref is a View); the L99 destructure with size='sm' default is preserved exactly (targetRef, ariaLabelEnter, ariaLabelExit, className renamed _className, size='sm', testHookSupported), plus the added style/testID. The local useTranslation() (L102) + supported state initializer (L103-105: testHookSupported!==undefined ? testHookSupported : probeSupport()) + isFs state (L106) are ported verbatim with identical state names (supported/isFs).

testHookSupported effect (L108-114) is ported verbatim: if testHookSupported is defined it setSupported(testHookSupported) and returns; otherwise setSupported(probeSupport()); deps [testHookSupported]. fullscreenchange sync effect (L116-135) is ported with structure preserved: the inner sync() reads targetRef.current + readFullscreenElement() and computes active = target!=null && el!=null && el===target, then setIsFs(active); sync() is invoked once. The web document.addEventListener('fullscreenchange', sync) subscription + removeEventListener cleanup (L131-134) have no native event source and are omitted (returns undefined); the L126-127 `target.contains(el)` descendant branch has no DOM analog on native refs and is omitted — both documented inline. The [targetRef] dependency is preserved so the effect is not flagged by exhaustive-deps.

toggle callback (L137-163) is ported: const target = targetRef.current; if (!target) return; (L138-139) is preserved as the null-guard. The exit/foreign-lock-release/request arbitration (L141-156) and the catch+console.warn rejection path (L157-162) have no React Native API to drive (no document.exitFullscreen, no target.requestFullscreen) and collapse to a documented native-safe no-op; deps [targetRef] preserved. The early-return-null when unsupported (L165) is ported verbatim (if (!supported) return null;), so by default the native button renders nothing.

Label computation (L167-169) is ported verbatim: enterLabel = ariaLabelEnter ?? t('common.fullscreen.enter','Enter fullscreen'); exitLabel = ariaLabelExit ?? t('common.fullscreen.exit','Exit fullscreen'); label = isFs ? exitLabel : enterLabel — i18n keys + English fallbacks retained for future wiring. The Button render (L171-194) -> a Pressable: variant='ghost' (L175) -> transparent fill + colors.surfaceHover pressed tint (web hover:bg-gray-100 dark:hover:bg-gray-800); size (L176-177) -> sizeStyles (sm !h-7!w-7!p-0=28x28 pad 0, md h-10 px-4=40/16, lg h-12 px-6=48/24) + rounded-md=6; cn(className) (L177) merged via the native style prop; the Maximize/Minimize icon swap (L178-184, h-3.5 w-3.5=14) -> AppText glyph '⤢'/'⤡' in the secondary text tone; onClick void toggle() (L185-187) -> onPress={toggle}.

Accessibility mapping (L188-192): aria-label (L188) + title (L190) -> accessibilityLabel; aria-pressed={isFs} (L189) -> accessibilityState={{selected: isFs}}; data-testid='fullscreen-button' (L191) -> testID (default 'fullscreen-button'); data-fullscreen-state on/off (L192) -> surfaced via accessibilityState.selected. The icon aria-hidden (L180/L182) is covered by the Pressable grouping its accessible label. The forced-colors:border / focus-visible:ring web affordances inherited from the Button host have no React Native analog and are intentionally omitted. The closing forwardRef bracket (L196) maps to the component close; FullscreenButton.displayName='FullscreenButton' is set and a default export added for native ergonomics.

No DOM-only modules, browser HTML elements, Recharts, Leaflet, lucide-react, react-i18next, cn, or old web UI components are imported (rule 4): only React + react-native (Pressable/StyleSheet/View + type StyleProp/ViewStyle) and the existing apps/native theme tokens + AppText primitive (rule 5). Gates run from apps/native: npm run typecheck (tsc --noEmit) exit 0; npm run lint -- --quiet (eslint @react-native) exit 0; npm test -- --runInBand --detectOpenHandles -> all existing suites pass (no regressions).
